title: Verifier-Guided Evaluation of LLM-Generated Network Configurations: a Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study evaluating whether a verifier-triggered guarded pipeline (generate → validate → repair, ≤1 repair) reduces deterministic-invariant violations versus single-shot initial generation for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a deterministic synthetic task generator and a deterministic network verifier, we ran 200 preregistered tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused for both baseline and guarded episodes) with the hosted model gpt-5-mini (archived model configuration records temperature = null/unset). Baseline configurations passed the verifier in 199/200 tasks (99.5%); the guarded pipeline passed 200/200 (100%). Paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005; discordant pairs n10 = 1, n01 = 0; exact two-sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The single guarded improvement resulted from one verifier-triggered repair correcting a multi-step ordering violation. We report the preregistration, execution accounting (including model-call accounting showing 200 shared initial calls + 1 repair call = 201 model calls), paired analysis, failure diagnosis, and bounded limitations (synthetic tasks, single model, and shared_initial_candidate semantics).

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configurations for network operations (NetOps). Operational safety requires that generated configurations satisfy deterministic invariants such as reachability, policy compliance, loop‑freedom, and ordered-change/workflow constraints. Prior work has developed intent→configuration prototypes and argued for verifier-integrated pipelines [1], and deterministic verifiers are available for configuration validation [2]. Cross-domain literature on generate→validate→repair patterns (program repair, tool-augmented agents) suggests that external validation can reduce unsafe outputs [4],[6]. Reporting and reproducibility guidelines for LLM studies further motivate preregistration and artifact disclosure [3].

This paper asks: under shared_initial_candidate semantics—where exactly one sampled initial generation per task is deterministically reused by both baseline and guarded episodes—does a verifier-triggered guarded pipeline (one permitted repair call) reduce invariant violations relative to single-shot generation? We tested this with a preregistered paired design (N = 200 tasks), a deterministic synthetic task generator, a deterministic network verifier, and the hosted LLM gpt-5-mini. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived.
sections.related_work: Intent→configuration research has produced prototype pipelines and task banks that assess whether models can synthesize device configurations from natural-language intents [1]. Formal network-verification work defines and enforces invariants such as reachability and policy compliance and provides deterministic checking tools [2]. Work in program repair and tool-augmented LLM agents documents the practical value of generate→validate→repair loops in other domains [4],[6]. Surveys and safety analyses highlight LLM failure modes (hallucination, adversarial confabulation) and recommend verifier stages and provenance control for operational deployments [5],[3]. Our study situates a tightly controlled, verifier-centered empirical test within these strands: rather than ranking models, we quantify the marginal effect of a verifier/repair stage under shared_initial_candidate execution semantics.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand: The study (CAND-2026-001) was preregistered before observing outcomes. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline — a per-task binary indicator that the deterministic verifier accepts the generated configuration (all specified invariants pass).

Sampling and tasks: 200 deterministic intent→configuration tasks were generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 targeting very_hard and extreme workflow patterns. Inclusion/exclusion rules and deterministic selection indices were fixed in the preregistration; no preregistered exclusions occurred.

Generation semantics, model configuration, and adapter: The preregistered generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate: exactly one initial generation was sampled per task and deterministically reused for both baseline and guarded episodes; independent first-pass generations per condition were not produced. The declared execution model was gpt-5-mini; the archived execution model_configuration records temperature = null/unset. We state explicitly that null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. The hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter orchestrated model calls and verifier interactions. The adapter allowed at most one automated repair call per task.

Verifier and scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 performed full intent-constraint validation: syntactic parsing, per-device allowed-field checks, encoded workflow/ordering policies, and network-level invariants. Per-task outcome is binary: 'all invariants pass' versus 'any invariant fails'. The scorer and all decision rules were deterministic and archived.

Model-call accounting (artifact-backed): The archived provider audit shows 201 hosted model calls used. This corresponds to 200 shared_initial_generation calls (one per task) plus 1 repair call invoked by the guarded pipeline (201 total). Under shared_initial_candidate semantics, baseline and guarded episodes reuse the same sampled initial candidate; the guarded-only model call occurs only when a repair is invoked. For artifact verification see the archived execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json) and the model-configuration and raw-results artifact entries in the archived bundle (paths and artifact-indexing are available in the manifest).
sections.results:
Execution accounting: The run completed per preregistration (planned episodes = 400; completed episodes = 400; model_calls_used = 201). The deterministic reconciliation artifact confirms complete_pair_count = 200 and stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1}.

Primary outcomes: baseline successes = 199/200 (0.995); guarded successes = 200/200 (1.0). Paired contingency: n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0 (rows: guarded; columns: baseline). Paired absolute risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The analysis used an exact two-sided McNemar implementation for small discordant counts (archived analytic output). The exact test yields p = 1.0 for n10 = 1 and n01 = 0; this p-value reflects the small-sample discrete nature of the exact test given a single discordant pair and should be interpreted alongside the observed discordant counts and bootstrap CI (see below). A paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the risk difference = [0.00, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729).

Repair activity and failure diagnosis: The guarded pipeline invoked its single permitted repair once; that repair converted the sole baseline failure into a guarded success. The archived validator trace for that task indicates a multi-step ordering/workflow violation (a required sequence breach across interfaces). The repair produced a corrected sequence that satisfied the verifier's encoded invariants and the verifier accepted the repaired candidate. Representative per-task scoring examples and validator traces are archived (see execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/ in the bundle).

Missingness and exclusions: No preregistered exclusions occurred; no persistent unparsable or failed episodes were observed under the prespecified handling rules.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation constrained by design: Because generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, baseline and guarded episodes began from the same sampled candidate; therefore the observed paired difference arises solely from verifier-triggered repair rather than independent first-pass generation differences or constrained prompting. The single repaired case corrected a workflow-ordering violation.

Statistical context and power: The preregistration planned to detect a 10–15 percentage-point absolute paired change with N = 200 assuming mid-range baseline rates (~45–65%). The observed baseline (~99.5%) was far higher than anticipated, so the original power assumptions do not apply; the study therefore lacks sensitivity to detect modest improvements beyond the single repaired case. The exact McNemar p = 1.0 is a natural consequence of one discordant pair (n10=1,n01=0) under the small-sample exact test implementation; the paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (0.015) quantifies the realized precision given these data.

Threats to validity and scope: Internal validity is constrained by shared_initial_candidate semantics (no independent first-pass contrast), by reliance on a single deterministic verifier implementation (its encoded invariants define the pass/fail outcome), and by a single-model evaluation. Construct validity: the verifier enforces encoded invariants but does not substitute for live-device execution or telemetry-sensitive checks. External validity: tasks are synthetic and the model set is narrow; adversarial contamination was not exercised. Practical implication: in this constrained synthetic corpus, a verifier gate with a bounded repair corrected a single multi-step ordering fault, but broader operational claims require multi-model evaluation, independent first-pass comparisons (if that estimand is of interest), adversarial testing, and live-device studies.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired evaluation of a verifier-guarded intent→configuration pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics. With gpt-5-mini on the supplied synthetic task bank, single-shot generation produced very high verifier compliance (199/200), and a single verifier-triggered repair converted the sole failing case into success, yielding a small absolute improvement (0.5 percentage points) with paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.00, 0.015]. The archived bundle documents the end-to-end generator→validator→repair pipeline and analysis artifacts. Future work should evaluate multiple models, larger and more diverse task banks (including noisy or partial state and live-device semantics), independent first-pass contrasts when required by the estimand, adversarial contamination testing, and richer runtime oracles.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: This run implemented preregistered study CAND-2026-001 and was executed autonomously after the autonomy lock. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (archived model_configuration records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling or temperature = 0). Orchestration adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). The preregistration fixed generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per task was deterministically reused by baseline and guarded episodes) and allowed at most one automated repair call per task. Model-call accounting in the archived execution manifest reflects 200 shared initial generation calls and 1 repair call (201 model calls total). All provider traces, verifier logs, task manifests, model-configuration records, and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle (see execution/execution_manifest.json for the manifest that indexes archived artifact paths). No human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Synthetic deterministic task bank and verifier: results reflect correctness under the chosen synthetic intent templates and deterministic verifier and do not guarantee similar performance on live heterogeneous production devices or telemetry.
Single-model experiment (gpt-5-mini): findings do not demonstrate multi-model generality.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded conditions began from the same initial generation; the study measures verifier/repair effects only and does not evaluate independent prompt-engineering or constrained-generation effects.
Limited adversarial/contamination testing: the run did not include systematic adversarial retrieval or poisoned-context attacks; such threats remain an open evaluation axis.

Oracle coverage: the deterministic verifier enforces encoded invariants but may omit runtime behaviors and device-specific semantics observable only through live execution; external validity to live deployments is therefore limited.
